review_notes: Reviewed all 106 lines and inspected the imported group-law proof, the ambient automorphism application lemma, and the proposed Mathlib derivative-shift lemma. The suggested replacement follows that lemma’s stated translation-invariance behavior; I have not claimed it was compiled.

have hshift : HasDerivAt (fun v : ℝ => v+t) 1 u := by simpa only [id_eq] using (hasDerivAt_id u).add_const t

findings.problem: This manually constructs the derivative of a translation and applies the chain rule, then simplifies the result back to the translated function. Mathlib provides a named lemma for exactly this operation.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the derivative component of the pair with `(hd x hxr (u+t) (hsum hu).1).hasDerivAt.comp_add_const u t`, leaving the second component unchanged. The surrounding pair can read `(fun u hu => ⟨(hd x hxr (u+t) (hsum hu).1).hasDerivAt.comp_add_const u t, (hρK (hstep₀ (u+t) (hsum hu).2 x hx₀)).1⟩)`.
findings.benefit: Removes the low-level chain-rule steps while retaining the mathematical idea: translating the input by a constant preserves the derivative. The named lemma makes that reason easier to recognize.
